text:
nicholas: heading to SFO tomorrow for the offsite — debating whether to book a lounge daypass or just crash in an airport nap pod for the 6-hour layover. pros/cons? :airplane:

maria: nap pods. 1) actually sleep 2) quiet 3) curtains > lounge background. bring earplugs + sleep mask. :zzz:

jon: lounge for showers + food. if you need to look alive at arrival, lounge > pod. :shower:

leo: agree with jon. also pods can be tiny — i'm 6'2" and could not stretch. check dimensions before booking.

sasha: pro-tip: Priority Pass + Amex Platinum often include lounges. check the app for day passes — sometimes cheaper than a pod.

ryan: if you choose pod, reserve in advance — airports often have only a handful. set an alarm and leave at least 90m before boarding.

ella: mini-poll — react :zzz: for pod, :coffee: for lounge, :thumbsup: for both? quick decide.

nicholas: ok i'm leaning pod. anyone tried the "sleep capsule" at BOS? curious about privacy and noise.

maria: BOS capsules are tight but good. white-noise app + thin travel blanket helped me sleep. also bring a small lock for the locker if you need gear.

jon: if you need to freshen up after, many lounges have showers and sinks — bring a tiny microfiber towel and a small deodorant stick.

leo: another weird one — some pods have outlets that are only USB-A. bring a USB-A cable or a short USB-C-to-A adapter. saved me once.

travel-bot: Reminder: team travel sheet updated — add your arrival times here: https://redwood.infra/travel/offsite-2026 — please fill by EOD.

nicholas: added my arrival. thanks all — booking pod now, lounge as backup. :thumbsup:
